    "LC": "The attacker-controlled invoice description is stored by the submission route and subsequently ingested through get_invoice_details, making this an indirect language-control path. The detector returns an advisory flag rather than transforming the description into independently validated fields (finbot-ctf-demo/src/routes/vendor.py:69-110; finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:363-407).",
    "CP": "Processing initializes a fresh message list, while the durable invoice description remains source content rather than standing agent memory (finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:163-166; finbot-ctf-demo/src/routes/vendor.py:69-110). The configuration-memory writer is not among the callable tools on this path, so its separate persistence vulnerability does not establish cross-session persistence here (finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:347-361; finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:735-748).",
    "AP": "Influence passes from the retrieval tool through FinBot's decision process to its approval tool under the same operating principal and policy domain (finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:150-226; finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:347-361). The database write is a subsequent-system impact, not evidence of intent propagating to another agent or principal.",
    "RH": "The approval tool can change the state evaluated by the CTF success checks and set the captured flag, placing an evaluator channel within the agent's reach (finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:409-443). The walkthrough supplies scenarios and refinement instructions, but no human-verified production-equivalent episode, supporting Possible rather than Demonstrated (finbot-ctf-demo/docs/FinBot-CTF-walkthrough-goal-manipulation.md:111-134).",
    "ES": "Tool identities are fixed, but their argument schemas are model-facing and dispatch does not independently validate or scope the model-selected invoice_id before approval (finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:228-345; finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:347-361; finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:409-443). This satisfies Wide's unconstrained-arguments branch despite the fixed callable list.",
    "CVSS": "The public network deployment and unauthenticated, synchronous registration/submission APIs establish AV:N, PR:N and UI:N; open CORS does not introduce a required victim action (finbot-ctf-demo/gunicorn.conf.py:4; finbot-ctf-demo/src/main.py:18; finbot-ctf-demo/src/routes/vendor.py:12-48; finbot-ctf-demo/src/routes/vendor.py:69-110). AC:L and AT:N apply because approval has no enforced amount or detector guard to defeat and no special execution condition is documented; the attacker owns the submitted vendor/invoice inputs, not CineFlow's approval authority (finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:363-407; finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:409-443). Unauthorized payment approval has serious integrity consequences for the agent's decision process and the separate SQLite store, supporting VI:H and SI:H, while this path establishes no confidentiality or availability loss (finbot-ctf-demo/docs/FinBot-CTF-walkthrough-goal-manipulation.md:86-91; finbot-ctf-demo/src/services/finbot_agent.py:409-443; finbot-ctf-demo/src/main.py:35-65)."
